en.full_desc:
Television production depends on more than cameras and a studio.

A show needs rhythm, timing, editorial clarity and a technical system that can perform consistently.

Presenters need direction. Guests need preparation. Every department needs to understand what is happening next, especially when the production is live.

Global Untold Story develops and produces television shows, digital formats and live broadcasts from the first concept through final delivery.

We can create a new format, produce a pilot, manage a complete season or join an existing production with the specific creative, editorial and technical support it requires.

We work across studio, field and hybrid production environments, building each workflow around the format, platform, audience and production scale.

TELEVISION FORMATS WE PRODUCE

Our production services can support:

Talk shows

Interview programs

News and current affairs formats

Magazine shows

Entertainment programs

Competition and game shows

Business and financial programs

Cultural and educational formats

Sports and gaming shows

Branded television formats

Government and institutional programs

Live specials

Digital studio shows

Remote and hybrid broadcasts

Field based factual programs

Concert and performance broadcasts

Talent led formats

Audience participation shows

Podcast and video podcast formats

Every format has its own production language.

A live interview show cannot be built like a game show, and a weekly digital series should not inherit an expensive television workflow it does not need.

We build the system around the show.

TV SHOW AND BROADCAST PRODUCTION CAPABILITIES

FORMAT AND SHOW DEVELOPMENT

A television show must be more than an idea that works once.

It needs a repeatable structure that can hold different guests, subjects and episodes without becoming predictable.

We help shape the format from the audience proposition through the episode structure.

Development can include:

Core show concept

Audience definition

Format structure

Segment development

Episode rhythm

Presenter role

Guest logic

Recurring features

Set and visual direction

Pilot structure

Season planning

Format bible

Digital extensions

Commercial integration opportunities

The goal is to create a show with a clear identity and enough flexibility to grow over time.

PILOT PRODUCTION

A pilot tests more than the concept.

It reveals whether the presenter works, whether the segments flow, whether the studio supports the format and whether the production can be repeated within the intended budget and schedule.

Pilot production can include:

Format refinement

Script and rundown development

Presenter testing

Guest booking

Set and studio planning

Graphics development

Rehearsals

Multi camera recording

Test transmission

Pilot editing

Internal review versions

Audience testing where required

Development recommendations

Updated production planning

The pilot should help decision makers understand what the show can become, not simply demonstrate that it can be filmed.

SEASON PLANNING AND PRODUCTION STRUCTURE

A successful episode is not enough if the production cannot sustain an entire season.

We design repeatable workflows covering editorial preparation, guest coordination, scripts, crew, studio time, rehearsals, recording, post production and delivery.

Season planning may include:

Episode calendars

Production schedules

Editorial deadlines

Guest booking systems

Crew structures

Studio planning

Budget frameworks

Approval workflows

Recording and delivery timelines

Archive organization

Quality control

Contingency planning

Season launch requirements

Digital publishing schedules

A strong production system protects consistency without making every episode feel identical.

RUNDOWNS, SCRIPTS AND EDITORIAL WORKFLOW

Live and recorded shows depend on a clear rundown.

Every segment needs a purpose, a duration and a defined transition into what follows. The production team must know what is happening while the presenter still feels natural on screen.

Our editorial support can include:

Episode rundowns

Presenter scripts

Introductions and links

Interview structures

Segment timing

Questions and talking points

Research briefs

Guest notes

Visual cue planning

Commercial break structure

Last minute editorial updates

Control room copies

Teleprompter scripts

Running order management

The rundown is not paperwork.

It is the map that keeps the entire production moving together.

STUDIO MULTI CAMERA PRODUCTION

Studio television requires close coordination between the floor and the control room.

Camera operators, sound, lighting, graphics, playback, presenters and producers all need to respond to the same live direction.

Our studio production support can include:

Multi camera direction

Camera planning

Vision mixing

Floor management

Stage management

Studio crews

Lighting coordination

Audio mixing

Playback systems

Teleprompters

Presenter monitoring

Recording and backup workflows

Studio audience coordination

Intercom and communication systems

We can work inside an existing studio or assemble the required production structure around the format.

LIVE DIRECTION AND CONTROL ROOM PRODUCTION

The control room is where the show becomes a broadcast.

Control room support can include:

Live directing

Vision mixing

Producer coordination

Timing control

Graphics cues

Playback cues

Camera communication

Presenter communication

Commercial break management

Remote contributor coordination

Recording supervision

Transmission coordination

Show calling

Live problem solving

The objective is controlled energy.

PRESENTER AND GUEST DIRECTION

The strongest technical production cannot rescue a weak on air performance.

Our support can include:

Presenter coaching

Format orientation

Script rehearsal

Teleprompter training

Interview technique

Timing and cue awareness

Live recovery techniques

Guest briefing

Panel moderation support

On camera feedback

Performance review

Ongoing season coaching

Chemistry testing

Presenter and guest rehearsals

Direction is adapted to the person.

FIELD PRODUCTION AND RECORDED PACKAGES

Many studio shows depend on material produced outside the studio.

Field reports, interviews, documentary packages and location segments give the program visual range and allow subjects to be explored beyond the conversation desk.

Field production can include:

Interviews

News packages

Presenter led segments

Documentary inserts

Location reports

Profiles and human stories

Behind the scenes coverage

Vox pops

Event based segments

Multi location filming

Archive integration

Remote contributor recordings

International field production

Pre recorded opening sequences

Each package is produced according to the tone, duration and editorial needs of the show.

LIVE BROADCASTING

A television program may need to reach audiences through several channels at the same time.

We can coordinate live outputs for television, digital platforms, private networks and branded channels while maintaining one connected production workflow.

Live delivery can support:

Television channels

YouTube

Facebook

LinkedIn

Digital and streaming platforms

Private websites

Internal networks

Remote viewing systems

Hybrid productions

Multiple digital outputs

Regional platform feeds

Recorded backup masters

The final structure depends on the studio, transmission route, platform requirements and available connectivity.

REMOTE GUESTS AND HYBRID PRODUCTION

Guests do not always need to be inside the studio.

Remote interviews and hybrid formats can expand access to contributors across different cities and countries, but they require careful preparation to avoid weak sound, inconsistent images and uncomfortable delays.

Support can include:

Remote guest testing

Connection checks

Camera and sound guidance

Remote contribution platforms

Return video

Presenter and guest communication

Live delay management

Backup connection planning

Remote recording

Visual consistency

Technical rehearsals

Hybrid control room workflows

Remote interpretation feeds

Contributor technical support

Remote contribution should feel like part of the show, not an interruption to it.

BROADCAST GRAPHICS AND SHOW IDENTITY

Graphics help the audience understand what they are watching and give the show a recognizable visual language.

We create graphics packages designed around the format, channel identity and technical workflow.

Graphics can include:

Show openers

Closing sequences

Lower thirds

Name straps

Topic titles

Stings

Transitions

Data graphics

Timelines

Maps

Social media integrations

On screen prompts

Sponsorship elements

Digital screen content

Scoreboards and voting graphics

Reusable episode templates

Every element is prepared according to the requirements of the control room, playback system and final delivery workflow.

SET DESIGN AND STUDIO VISUAL DIRECTION

The set is part of the format.

Its scale, layout, screens, seating and lighting all influence how the show feels and how efficiently it can be produced.

Studio visual support can include:

Set concept development

Production design

Desk and seating layouts

Screen planning

Background content

Lighting direction

Camera movement planning

Branding integration

Presenter positions

Guest positions

Audience layouts

Temporary studio builds

Modular set systems

Virtual and extended set elements

The design must look strong on camera while supporting the practical needs of the show.

BROADCAST AUDIO

Television audiences may tolerate an imperfect image before they tolerate unclear sound.

Broadcast audio planning may include:

Presenter microphones

Guest microphones

Panel sound

Audience microphones

Music playback

Remote guest audio

Studio ambience

Communication systems

Audio mixing

Recording and backup feeds

Final broadcast mix

Post production sound

Simultaneous interpretation feeds

Multi language audio routing

Every speaker should be heard clearly, regardless of how complex the studio becomes.

RECORDING, INGEST AND MEDIA MANAGEMENT

Television production generates a large volume of material.

Without a clear recording and archive system, footage becomes difficult to locate, reuse or repurpose.

Our workflow can include:

Program recording

Isolated camera recording

Clean feeds

Graphics feeds

Audio splits

File naming

Media ingest

Backup copies

Episode folders

Archive organization

Delivery tracking

Long term content libraries

Metadata organization

Version control

A structured archive allows the production to reuse interviews, packages and key moments across future episodes and digital content.

POST PRODUCTION AND EPISODE FINISHING

Not every program is transmitted live, and even live shows often require edited versions.

Our post production team can manage:

Episode editing

Segment editing

Timing adjustments

Highlight packages

Social media clips

Color correction

Sound editing

Graphics integration

Music

Promos and teasers

Clean versions

Final mastering

Quality control

Platform versions

International versions

Episode archive masters

The editorial style remains consistent across the season while allowing each episode to find its own energy.

PROMOS, CUTDOWNS AND DIGITAL EXTENSIONS

A show should continue reaching audiences after the original broadcast.

We can transform episodes into shorter content designed for digital discovery, social sharing and future promotion.

Deliverables can include:

Episode promos

Coming up clips

Best moments

Interview highlights

Short vertical edits

Topic based clips

Presenter clips

Guest quotes

Social teasers

YouTube versions

Reels and short form content

Season trailers

Podcast versions

Behind the scenes content

Sponsor cutdowns

This gives the program a wider content life without weakening the main broadcast.

LOCALIZATION AND INTERNATIONAL DELIVERY

Programs designed for regional or international audiences may require several language and delivery versions.

Localization services can include:

Arabic and English subtitles

Multilingual subtitles

Closed captions

Voice over

Dubbing

Dialogue replacement

Script adaptation

Graphics replacement

Textless masters

International delivery files

Platform specific versions

Archive packages

Multi language audio versions

Localized promos and cutdowns

Localization should be considered early so that later versions remain consistent and efficient.

LIVE PRODUCTION RELIABILITY

Live television depends on preparation.

Every technical system has potential points of failure, so important productions require backup thinking before transmission begins.

Depending on the show, the production plan may consider:

Technical rehearsals

Backup recordings

Isolated camera feeds

Alternative playback files

Audio backups

Power protection

Communication systems

Presenter recovery plans

Replacement segments

Emergency timing options

Remote guest backups

Transmission contingencies

Alternative connection routes

Backup graphics and media

Escalation procedures

No live production is completely risk free.

Strong preparation gives the team more ways to protect the broadcast when something changes.

FROM ONE SHOW TO A COMPLETE MEDIA PROPERTY

A strong format can become more than a television program.

With the right structure, one show can generate:

Full episodes

Digital clips

Podcast versions

Social media content

Behind the scenes material

Sponsor integrations

Live audience extensions

Newsletter content

Archive libraries

Regional adaptations

Branded segments

Future seasons

Format licensing opportunities

Live events

Talent led extensions

We can help design the show as a repeatable media property rather than a sequence of disconnected episodes.

WHY WORK WITH GLOBAL UNTOLD STORY?

We understand television from both sides of the camera.

Our team combines creative development, live direction, presenter support, technical planning, field production and post production within one connected workflow.

Clients bring us in when they need:

A show developed from concept to broadcast

A pilot designed to prove the format

Experienced multi camera and control room production

Strong timing and live direction

Presenter and guest support

Studio and field production under one team

Arabic and English production communication

Broadcast and digital outputs

Repeatable systems for episodes and seasons

Regional experience with international production standards

A partner prepared to think beyond the immediate production

We do not treat television as an event with cameras.

We build the editorial, technical and human system that allows a show to return week after week.

WHAT WE NEED TO PREPARE A PROPOSAL

To understand the show and prepare the right production approach, it is helpful to receive:

Show concept

Intended audience

Channel or platform

Live or recorded format

Episode duration

Number of episodes

Studio requirements

Presenter and guest structure

Required field segments

Graphics requirements

Transmission requirements

Delivery formats

Production dates

Launch schedule

Required languages

Digital content requirements

Available format materials

Budget guidance where available

A complete format bible is not essential.

We can join while the show is still being shaped.

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

DO YOU PROVIDE COMPLETE TV SHOW PRODUCTION SERVICES?

Yes. We can support format development, pilot production, studio recording, live direction, field segments, graphics, post production and final delivery.

DO YOU PRODUCE TV SHOWS INTERNATIONALLY?

Yes. We can build productions across regional and international markets through project specific crews, studios and local production partnerships where required.

CAN YOU DEVELOP A NEW TELEVISION FORMAT?

Yes. We can help shape the concept, audience proposition, segments, presenter role, episode structure and season workflow.

CAN YOU PRODUCE A PILOT EPISODE?

Yes. We can plan and produce a pilot to test the format, presenter, studio, timing, visual identity and production requirements.

DO YOU PROVIDE MULTI CAMERA STUDIO PRODUCTION?

Yes. We provide multi camera direction, camera crews, vision mixing, floor management, audio, lighting and control room coordination.

CAN YOU DIRECT LIVE TELEVISION?

Yes. We can provide live directing, timing control, graphics and playback cues, presenter communication and production coordination.

DO YOU COACH PRESENTERS?

Yes. We support presenters with rehearsal, teleprompter use, interview technique, live timing and on air performance.

CAN YOU PRODUCE FIELD REPORTS AND RECORDED PACKAGES?

Yes. We produce interviews, reports, documentary inserts, profiles and presenter led location segments.

CAN YOU BROADCAST ON TELEVISION AND DIGITAL PLATFORMS AT THE SAME TIME?

Yes, depending on the available technical infrastructure and platform requirements. We can coordinate television and digital outputs through one production workflow.

DO YOU CREATE COMPLETE SHOW GRAPHICS?

Yes. We produce openers, lower thirds, transitions, topic graphics, titles, data graphics and complete visual packages.

CAN YOU WORK INSIDE AN EXISTING STUDIO?

Yes. We can work with an existing studio and technical team or assemble additional production resources according to the requirements of the format.

CAN YOU PRODUCE RECURRING EPISODES OR A COMPLETE SEASON?

Yes. We can build repeatable editorial, studio, recording, post production and delivery workflows for recurring productions.

DO YOU PROVIDE POST PRODUCTION AND SOCIAL MEDIA CUTDOWNS?

Yes. We edit episodes, promos, highlights and short digital content in multiple durations and formats.

CAN YOU INTEGRATE REMOTE GUESTS?

Yes. We can coordinate testing, technical preparation, contribution platforms, return feeds, recording and live integration for remote participants.

CAN YOU LOCALIZE SHOWS FOR DIFFERENT MARKETS?

Yes. We provide subtitles, captions, voice over, dubbing, graphics replacement and multilingual delivery.

HOW MUCH DOES TV SHOW PRODUCTION COST?

The budget depends on the format, number and duration of episodes, studio requirements, crew structure, set, graphics, field production, transmission and post production scope.

Sharing the concept and expected production model allows us to recommend a realistic structure and budget direction.

HOW LONG DOES IT TAKE TO DEVELOP AND PRODUCE A SHOW?

The timeline depends on the development stage, format complexity, pilot requirements, studio availability, presenter and guest preparation, graphics and number of episodes.

A pilot can move faster than a complete season, while live or technically complex formats require additional testing and rehearsal.

BUILD THE SHOW BEFORE THE RED LIGHT COMES ON

Whether you are developing a talk show, studio format, live special or digital program, we can build the creative, editorial and technical production around the idea.

Share the concept, episode structure, intended platform and production requirements. Our team will review the brief and respond within one business day with the right questions and next steps.
